questions.question:
Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.

Credit cards are replacing cash transactions.

options.text: Cash transactions are replaced by credit cards.
Cash transactions have been replaced by credit cards.
Cash transactions are being replaced by credit cards.
Cash transactions had been replaced by credit cards.

questions.solution:
**The correct answer is option 3.**

*Cash transactions **are being replaced** by credit cards.*

While changing from active to passive form, we interchange the subject and the object of the sentence. The given sentence is in present continuous tense identified by **are replacing** so, we change the form of the main verb to the past participle form i.e **replaced** and add **being.**

So, options** 1,2 and 4 **are** incorrect.**

questions.question:
**Select the correct active form of the given sentence.**

We were given very little time to prepare the presentation.

options.text: They have given us very little time to prepare the presentation.
They give us very little time to prepare the presentation.
They will give us very little time to prepare the presentation.
They gave us very little time to prepare the presentation.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__They gave us very little time to prepare the presentation.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2b32682084110076f9f927b52d79b0ad5c22d4f728ac3c21d1be492f4572e5d4.png] 

 
• In **Active Voice**, a sentence emphasizes the subject, performing an action.
 
• In **Passive Voice**, a sentence emphasizes the action or the object of the sentence.
 
• The **given sentence** is in the **passive voice** and '**We**' is the **subject **and the **object **is hidden**.**
 
• When we convert this sentence into **active voice**, the subject '**We**' of the **passive voice** becomes the** object (objective case for 'we' is 'us')**, the hidden **object **'**they**' becomes the **subject**.
 
• The passive format **"were + V3 (given)"** should be changed into the active format **"V2 (gave)"**.
 
• This is the active and passive voice **rule** for the **past simple tense**.
 
• **Hence**, the correct answer is** option 4**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a0ae0382de38c61e45ed884c7ca9688b47148fce0fe8e249cd313ced26c2c6ee.png]

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank No.(1)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"Originated."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The verb "originated" refers to the point or place where something begins, arises, or is derived. This fits perfectly in the context of describing where the English language originally comes from.
 
• English, as known historically, originated in what is now England; it did not originate in India. This makes "originated" the most appropriate choice to convey that English was not native to India.
 
• The sentence structure requires a verb that indicates the beginning or source of the English language, and "originated" correctly fulfills this requirement.
 
• Using "originated" correctly establishes the distinction between English and indigenous languages of India.
 
 
• Example: Think of a popular game like Cricket which originated in England but is played and loved in India. Similarly, English originated (or started) in Britain but is widely used in India today.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Option 2, "derived," is incorrect as it suggests that English was directly obtained from another source, which is not the intended meaning in this context.
 
• Option 3, "developed," might imply that English evolved independently in India, which is not accurate.
 
• Option 4, "created," is also incorrect as it would imply English was invented in India, which is historically inaccurate.
